```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Model: `PeneDumitrescu_2016_umeclidinium`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("PeneDumitrescu_2016_umeclidinium"))$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("PeneDumitrescu_2016_umeclidinium"))$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12406> (PMC5351336)

Umeclidinium (UMEC), a long-acting muscarinic antagonist marketed as an inhaled
COPD therapy, was studied as a topical treatment for primary hyperhidrosis.
Healthy men received a single dose of [14C]UMEC solution on one axilla or palm
for 8 h, and plasma [14C]UMEC was measured by accelerator mass spectrometry
(AMS). Only the occluded-axilla cohort had enough quantifiable concentrations
for modelling. Because UMEC kinetics after dermal dosing are absorption-rate
limited, those data were pooled with 30-min intravenous infusion data from a
prior study so that absorption and disposition could be separated. The final
model (Figure 2 of the paper) is two-compartment with linear elimination and
two sequential absorption processes: a fraction F1 of the bioavailable dermal
dose enters the central compartment at a constant rate, and the remainder is
absorbed first-order from a skin pool after the lag time Tlag.

No correction notice for the article was registered with CrossRef, and none
was found on Europe PMC, as of 2026-11-25.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("PeneDumitrescu_2016_umeclidinium"))$population
str(pop[c("species", "n_subjects", "n_studies", "age_range", "weight_mean", "sex_female_pct")])
```

The modelling dataset held 15 subjects: the 6 healthy men of the
occluded-axilla cohort (Table 1: mean age 47.8 years, range 30-55; mean weight
82.9 kg; mean BMI 26.0 kg/m2; all White) and 9 subjects given 65 ug UMEC as a
30-min intravenous infusion in study NCT01110018, whose demographics the paper
does not report. Each dermal subject received 165 mg of a 1.85% (w/w) solution
(about 3.06 mg UMEC) over 40 cm2 of one axilla under an occlusive dressing,
washed off after 8 h. Covariate effects were not investigated.

| `lq` | CL2 = 40.9 L/h | Table 3 |

# Dosing records

A dermal administration is two records at the same time with the same amount:
one into `depot` (the first-order part, `f(depot) = F * (1 - F1)`, starting
after `tlag`) and one into `central` with `rate = -2`, so that rxode2 applies
the modelled zero-order duration (`f(central) = F * F1`). The intravenous dose
is one infusion into `central` with an explicit rate and `ROUTE_IV = 1`, which
sets `f(central)` to 1.

```{r events}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("PeneDumitrescu_2016_umeclidinium"))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

dose_derm <- 3060 # ug UMEC: 165 mg x 1.85% (Methods 'Treatments', ~3.06 mg)
dose_iv <- 65 # ug over 0.5 h (Results)
loq <- 0.348 # pg/mL (Methods 'Analytical methods')

make_events <- function(ids, route, obs_times) {
  if (route == "dermal") {
    dose <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose_derm, rate = 0, cmt = "depot", evid = 1L),
      data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose_derm, rate = -2, cmt = "central", evid = 1L)
    )
    route_iv <- 0L
  } else {
    dose <- data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose_iv, rate = dose_iv / 0.5, cmt = "central", evid = 1L)
    route_iv <- 1L
  }
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times)
  obs <- data.frame(id = obs$id, time = obs$time, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central", evid = 0L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(ROUTE_IV = route_iv) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

# Typical-value checks

These checks compare deterministic typical-value solves against closed forms
that share the same parameters, so tight tolerances are appropriate.

```{r typical}
th <- mod$theta
CL <- exp(th[["lcl"]])
V1 <- exp(th[["lvc"]])
Q <- exp(th[["lq"]])
V2 <- exp(th[["lvp"]])
TLAG <- exp(th[["ltlag"]])
FD <- exp(th[["lfdepot"]])
F1 <- 1 - plogis(th[["logitffo"]])

t_iv <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2, 400, by = 0.5))))
t_derm <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 30, by = 0.05), seq(30, 1000, by = 1))))
sim_iv_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, make_events(1L, "iv", t_iv), returnType = "data.frame")
sim_derm_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, make_events(1L, "dermal", t_derm), returnType = "data.frame")

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
# AUC(0-inf) * CL must equal the bioavailable dose. Doses are in ug, CL in L/h
# and Cc in pg/mL, so AUC [pg*h/mL] / 1000 * CL [L/h] is in ug.
recov_iv <- trap(sim_iv_typ$time, sim_iv_typ$Cc) / 1000 * CL / dose_iv
recov_derm <- trap(sim_derm_typ$time, sim_derm_typ$Cc) / 1000 * CL / (FD * dose_derm)

# Before Tlag only the zero-order input acts: a constant-rate infusion of
# F * F1 * dose over Tlag into a two-compartment model, which has a closed form.
k10 <- CL / V1
k12 <- Q / V1
k21 <- Q / V2
s <- k10 + k12 + k21
alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
R0 <- FD * F1 * dose_derm / TLAG
c_inf <- function(t) {
  1000 * R0 / V1 * ((alpha - k21) / ((alpha - beta) * alpha) * (1 - exp(-alpha * t)) +
    (k21 - beta) / ((alpha - beta) * beta) * (1 - exp(-beta * t)))
}
early <- sim_derm_typ |> dplyr::filter(time > 0, time < TLAG)
rel_err <- max(abs(early$Cc / c_inf(early$time) - 1))

data.frame(
  check = c(
    "IV: AUC(0-inf) x CL / dose",
    "Dermal: AUC(0-inf) x CL / (F x dose)",
    "Dermal, t < Tlag: max relative error vs zero-order closed form"
  ),
  value = signif(c(recov_iv, recov_derm, rel_err), 4)
) |> knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  abs(recov_iv - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(recov_derm - 1) < 0.01,
  rel_err < 1e-3
)
```

The intravenous check also confirms that the dermal bioavailability is not
applied to the infusion (it would otherwise recover 0.3% of the dose), and the
early-phase check confirms that the zero-order input runs over `tlag` rather
than as a bolus.

```{r typical-plot, fig.cap = "Typical-value profiles after the dermal dose (3.06 mg to the occluded axilla) and the 65 ug i.v. infusion."}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(sim_derm_typ, route = "Dermal, occluded axilla (3.06 mg)"),
  dplyr::mutate(sim_iv_typ, route = "IV 65 ug over 0.5 h")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 96) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~route, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "UMEC concentration (pg/mL)")
```

# Visual predictive check (Figure 3e)

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160615)
n_per_arm <- 200
grid_iv <- c(seq(0.05, 1, by = 0.05), seq(1.25, 6, by = 0.25))
grid_derm <- c(seq(0.5, 24, by = 0.5), seq(25, 80, by = 1))
sim_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, make_events(seq_len(n_per_arm), "iv", grid_iv), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(route = "IV"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, make_events(n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm), "dermal", grid_derm), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(route = "Dermal")
)
vpc_q <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(route, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3e of Pene Dumitrescu 2016: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of simulated concentrations (with residual error) after the i.v. infusion (left) and the dermal dose (right). The dotted line is the AMS LOQ."}
vpc_q |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p05, p50, p95), names_to = "pct", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, linetype = pct)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = loq, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(p05 = "dotted", p50 = "solid", p95 = "dashed")) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(route, levels = c("IV", "Dermal")), scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "UMEC concentration (pg/mL)", linetype = "Percentile")
```

```{r vpc-table}
vpc_q |>
  dplyr::filter(
    (route == "IV" & time %in% c(0.5, 1, 2, 6)) |
      (route == "Dermal" & time %in% c(2, 8, 16, 24, 48, 72, 80))
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(p05, p50, p95), \(x) formatC(x, format = "g", digits = 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Route" = route, "Time (h)" = time,
    "5th pct (pg/mL)" = p05, "Median (pg/mL)" = p50, "95th pct (pg/mL)" = p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated percentiles at selected times.")
```

In the published Figure 3e (dermal panel), the simulated median starts near
2 pg/mL, declines to roughly 0.13 pg/mL at 80 h and the 95th percentile runs
from about 15-20 pg/mL down to about 4-5 pg/mL; in the i.v. panel the median
is about 1000-2000 pg/mL at the end of infusion and about 20 pg/mL at 6 h.
The simulated percentiles above follow the same course.

```{r vpc-check}
med_at <- function(r, t) vpc_q$p50[vpc_q$route == r & vpc_q$time == t]
stopifnot(
  med_at("IV", 0.5) > 500, med_at("IV", 0.5) < 3000,
  med_at("Dermal", 2) > 0.8, med_at("Dermal", 2) < 5,
  med_at("Dermal", 80) > 0.04, med_at("Dermal", 80) < 0.4
)
```

# Zero-order duration: why it equals Tlag

Table 3 has no separate duration parameter for the zero-order input. The paper
calls the absorption processes "sequential" (Abstract; Results), which with a
single time parameter means the zero-order input lasts until the first-order
input starts, i.e. for Tlag. A plausible alternative is that the zero-order
input lasts for the 8-h application. The chunk below simulates both readings
with the same virtual subjects and compares their dermal percentiles with
Figure 3e.

```{r duration-alt}
mod_alt <- mod |> rxode2::model(dur(central) <- 8)
grid_cmp <- c(2, 8, 16, 80)
ev_cmp <- make_events(seq_len(n_per_arm), "dermal", grid_cmp)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160616)
sim_tlag <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cmp, returnType = "data.frame")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160616)
sim_8h <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_alt, ev_cmp, returnType = "data.frame")
dur_cmp <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(sim_tlag, reading = "duration = Tlag (packaged)"),
  dplyr::mutate(sim_8h, reading = "duration = 8 h")
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(reading, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")
dur_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(p05, p50), \(x) formatC(x, format = "g", digits = 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Reading" = reading, "Time (h)" = time, "5th pct (pg/mL)" = p05, "Median (pg/mL)" = p50) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dermal percentiles (no residual error) under the two readings of the zero-order duration.")
```

```{r duration-check}
q_of <- function(reading_lab, t, col) dur_cmp[[col]][dur_cmp$reading == reading_lab & dur_cmp$time == t]
tl <- "duration = Tlag (packaged)"
h8 <- "duration = 8 h"
stopifnot(
  # Tlag reading: no early peak, low 5th percentile early on (as in Figure 3e)
  q_of(tl, 8, "p50") / q_of(tl, 2, "p50") < 1.3,
  q_of(tl, 2, "p05") < 0.7,
  # 8-h reading: a clear peak at 8 h and a high early 5th percentile
  q_of(h8, 8, "p50") / q_of(h8, 2, "p50") > 1.4,
  q_of(h8, 2, "p05") > 0.9
)
```

With an 8-h duration the median rises to a peak at 8 h and the 5th
percentile is about 1 pg/mL or more during the first hours, whereas the
published Figure 3e shows a median with no peak (near 2 pg/mL early, then
declining) and a 5th percentile near 0.3 pg/mL early on. The Tlag reading
reproduces both features and is the one packaged.

# Noncompartmental analysis (Table 2)

The observed noncompartmental parameters come from six subjects with AMS
sampling at 0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 8.5, 9, 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 24, 30,
36, 48 and 72 h. The simulation uses the same schedule with residual error,
drops concentrations below the 0.348 pg/mL LOQ (time zero is kept as 0) and
summarises Cmax and AUC(0-t) by their geometric means and Tmax by its median,
as Table 2 does.

```{r nca}
t_nca <- c(0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 8.5, 9, 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 24, 30, 36, 48, 72)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160617)
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, make_events(seq_len(n_per_arm), "dermal", t_nca), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = "Occluded axilla",
    conc = dplyr::if_else(time == 0, 0, sim)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc), time == 0 | conc >= loq) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, conc, treatment)

dose_nca <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_per_arm), time = 0, dose = dose_derm, treatment = "Occluded axilla")
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast"), !is.na(PPORRES))

geo <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x[x > 0])))
nca_sum <- nca_ind |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    PPORRES = if (dplyr::first(PPTESTCD) == "tmax") median(PPORRES) else geo(PPORRES),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

reference <- data.frame(treatment = "Occluded axilla", cmax = 7.92, tmax = 11.0, auclast = 113.7)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_sum,
  reference = reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "pg/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "pg*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated (n = 200) vs. observed (Table 2, n = 6) noncompartmental parameters",
  "after the occluded-axilla dose: geometric-mean Cmax and AUC(0-t), median Tmax.",
  "* differs by >20%."
))
```

```{r nca-check}
sim_of <- function(p) nca_sum$PPORRES[nca_sum$PPTESTCD == p]
stopifnot(
  nrow(nca_sum) == 3,
  # Geometric means of a 200-subject cohort: the envelope allows for the
  # sampling error of the very variable simulated exposures.
  abs(log(sim_of("cmax") / reference$cmax)) < log(1.5),
  abs(log(sim_of("auclast") / reference$auclast)) < log(1.5)
)
```

The simulated geometric-mean Cmax and AUC(0-t) and the median Tmax agree with
Table 2. The observed values come from only six subjects with between-subject
CVs of 333% (Cmax) and 407% (AUC(0-t)), so the agreement is closer than the
data could guarantee. AUC(0-inf) and half-life were calculable in only one
observed subject (702.5 pg*h/mL, 109 h) and are not compared.

# Steady state after daily application to both axillae (Figure 4)

Figure 4 simulates 14 daily applications of 2 mg/cm2 of the 1.85% solution to
both occluded axillae of men and women, with axilla areas drawn from published
measurements (Supplementary Information) and parameter uncertainty. Those area
distributions are not printed, so Figure 4 cannot be replicated exactly. The
chunk below uses the study's 40 cm2 template on each axilla
(2 x 40 x 2 mg x 1.85% = 2.96 mg UMEC/day) as an illustration.

```{r ss}
dose_ss <- 2 * 40 * 2 * 0.0185 * 1000 # ug/day
ids <- seq_len(n_per_arm)
ev_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = 14), time = rep(0:13 * 24, n_per_arm), amt = dose_ss, rate = 0, cmt = "depot", evid = 1L),
  data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = 14), time = rep(0:13 * 24, n_per_arm), amt = dose_ss, rate = -2, cmt = "central", evid = 1L),
  data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = 25), time = rep(13 * 24 + 0:24, n_per_arm), amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central", evid = 0L)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ROUTE_IV = 0L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160618)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_ss, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 13 * 24) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
typ_cavg <- 1000 * exp(th[["lfdepot"]]) * dose_ss / (CL * 24)
# Figure 4 median ~10-14 pg/mL is roughly twice the typical Cavg of this dose.
stopifnot(typ_cavg > 5, typ_cavg < 7.5)
```

```{r ss-plot, fig.cap = "Day-14 profile after daily application of 2 mg/cm2 to two 40-cm2 areas (illustrative dose); compare Figure 4 of Pene Dumitrescu 2016."}
sim_ss |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p05, p50, p95), names_to = "pct", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, conc, linetype = pct)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(p05 = "dashed", p50 = "solid", p95 = "dotted")) +
  labs(x = "Time after the day-14 dose (h)", y = "UMEC concentration (pg/mL)", linetype = "Percentile")
```

The typical steady-state average concentration for this illustrative dose is
`r signif(typ_cavg, 3)` pg/mL. Figure 4's median runs at about 10-14 pg/mL, so
its simulated doses were on average about twice this one, which corresponds
to roughly twice the 40 cm2 template area per axilla. The spread between the
5th and 95th percentiles spans about two orders of magnitude in both, as the
large between-subject variability in clearance and absorption implies.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Zero-order duration.** Table 3 lists no duration for the zero-order input;
  it is set equal to Tlag because the processes are described as sequential
  and the published VPC (Figure 3e) is reproduced with this reading but not
  with an 8-h duration (see the section above).
* **Final estimates vs bootstrap medians.** The model uses the "Model
  parameter estimates" column of Table 3. Several bootstrap medians differ
  noticeably (Tlag 4.71 h, F1 0.171, F 0.00217); the Discussion's "absolute
  bioavailability of 0.22%" is the bootstrap median of F, not the final
  estimate of 0.275%.
* **IIV scale.** Table 3 reports IIV as CV% of exponential random effects; the
  variances are omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). No covariances are reported, so the
  random effects are independent. V2, F and F1 have no IIV.
* **Bioavailability on the shared compartment.** The i.v. dose and the
  zero-order dermal input both enter the central compartment (Figure 2). The
  covariate `ROUTE_IV` sets the central-compartment bioavailability to 1 for
  the infusion and to F x F1 for the dermal input.
* **Dermal dose.** The modelled dose is the 3.06 mg of UMEC applied; the model
  does not represent the removal of unabsorbed drug at 8 h, which the paper's
  model also does not include.
* **IV cohort demographics** (NCT01110018) are not reported in the paper.
* **Below-LOQ handling.** The paper's population-model handling of
  nonquantifiable data is in the Supplementary Information and is not part of
  the packaged model; the NCA comparison above follows the Figure 1 rules
  approximately by dropping simulated values below the LOQ.
